reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an easy AVAX flash-loan arbitrage method and directs viewers to connect MetaMask, deploy a smart contract through Remix, and transfer $200 AVAX. The speaker claims this process can rapidly increase about $200 to about $1,775 through trading that inflates the coin's value. The contract behavior and claimed outcome are not verified by the disclaimer or supplied records.

citations.quote: How To Earn AVAX Easily Using Flash loans Arbitrage On Metamask Avalanche Works Perfectly 2022
you will see how to setup an arbitrage attack on two DEXs
On Deploy, Enter your token details and deploy the contract
Send $200 of Avalanche/AVAX to the contract for gas fee for all swaps
Call ‘flashloan’ function in Remix

opening.argument: The material expressly presents itself with a risk warning rather than a guarantee. It says, “This worked for me. But TRY IT AT YOUR OWN RISK,” which tells viewers that the outcome is uncertain and that they must make their own decision. The description also identifies the activity as a specific technical process involving AVAX, MetaMask, and a contract, not a promise that every viewer will profit. A cautious demonstration accompanied by an explicit warning is better characterized as operational education than deceptive certification of returns.

citations.quote: This worked for me. But TRY IT AT YOUR OWN RISK.
In this video, you can see how I used Flashloans to Arbitrage in Avalanche Mainnet by deploying Contract/Token to mask our arbitrage attack against Pangolin.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The warning is not contradicted by the instructions. Telling viewers to fund a contract and call a function describes how to reproduce the demonstration; it does not itself establish a guaranteed return. The prosecution's selected quotes emphasize the mechanics while omitting the express warning that the method worked for the speaker but remains at the viewer's own risk.

citations.quote: This worked for me. But TRY IT AT YOUR OWN RISK.
Call ‘flashloan’ function in Remix

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer cannot neutralize the video's concrete inducement. The same description tells viewers to send $200 AVAX to the contract, while the narration reports a dramatic increase from roughly $200 to a much larger amount. Calling the result “at your own risk” does not explain why the process should be expected to work for viewers or verify that the contract is safe.

opening.argument: The observable format is a technical demonstration in developer tooling. The speaker explains creating a Solidity file, changing the compiler, compiling it, connecting MetaMask, and deploying a contract; the sampled frames show Remix IDE, Solidity code, deployment controls, and wallet interactions. The description likewise organizes the material as numbered setup steps. That is consistent with teaching an operational workflow and showing one personal experiment, rather than selling membership, collecting credentials, or presenting a regulated investment service.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the activity an “attack” describes the demonstrated arbitrage technique, not the creator's relationship with the audience. The supplied material is dominated by code, compiler, wallet, and transaction steps, and even links to an explanation of flash loans. Those are hallmarks of a technical walkthrough; the existence of a profit claim does not by itself change the video's instructional format.

citations.quote: Smart Contract Code Link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical presentation does not make the promotion benign. The tutorial gives viewers a complete path to deploy the contract, fund it, and activate the flash loan, while the title says AVAX can be earned easily and that the method works perfectly. The code interface therefore serves as the delivery mechanism for a purported high-return result, not merely neutral instruction.

citations.quote: How To Earn AVAX Easily Using Flash loans Arbitrage On Metamask Avalanche Works Perfectly 2022
On Deploy, Enter your token details and deploy the contract
Call ‘flashloan’ function in Remix

opening.argument: The supplied workflow lacks several features normally associated with a deceptive financial solicitation. It does not ask viewers to surrender a password, buy a membership, recruit others, or pay a fee to an operator. Instead, the described funds are identified as AVAX held in the user's own wallet and as gas for swaps, while the process uses a smart contract and a flash-loan function. The evidence therefore supports a risky technical operation, but does not establish a hidden credential request, downline scheme, or guaranteed deposit-return mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution labels the transfer as suspicious without showing that the money goes to the creator or that viewers receive a promised payout. The stated purpose is gas for swaps, and the speaker even warns viewers to verify that MetaMask is connected to an on-chain contract. A transfer required to execute a technical transaction is not automatically evidence of a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Send $200 of Avalanche/AVAX to the contract for gas fee for all swaps
You don't want to fund a contract not on chain is what I am saying.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a password or recruitment scheme is beside the point. The relevant mechanism is a request to transfer substantial AVAX into a contract before activating a purported profit process. The narration then presents a spectacular result, saying the amount rose from $200 to $1,775. That combination is enough to make the funded-contract return claim central, even without additional scam features.
